item.title: German Chancellor Merz calls state election a 'disaster' for his party but vows to stay on
item.description:
Far-right AfD wins in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and leftwing Die Linke on course for victory in Berlin Germany’s embattled chancellor, Friedrich Merz, has vowed to stay in office and fight for future-proofing economic changes despite heavy losses for his conservatives in two state elections, one to the far right and the other to a leftwing party. Preliminary results indicated Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU) tallied just 4.9%, below ⁠the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament and indicating they may be excluded altogether. It would be the CDU’s worst-ever state score, which Merz called a “disaster”. Continue reading...

item.title: Macron, Carney hail new chapter in France-Canada ties at symbolic archipelago meeting
item.description:
Two leaders meet in French territory off Canada as Ottawa seeks stronger relations with EU while fighting trade war with US The leaders of France and Canada have pledged closer ties to grapple with rising geopolitical tensions, climate change and the erosion of democratic values, after ⁠they met in a ⁠French territory off Canada’s Atlantic coast. The two leaders’ visit to Saint-Pierre and Miquelon – the first by a French president since 2014 and the first by a Canadian prime minister – came just weeks ⁠after Donald Trump posted an image showing the islands, as well as all of Canada and other countries in North America, covered by the US flag. item.title: Iran war live: Tehran warns US against new strikes; fighting rages in Yemen
item.description:
Russia had its infamous " three-day special military operation " in Ukraine. America now has its " short-term excursion " into Iran. In February 2026, when he chose to start the war, President Donald Trump promised the public that it would last only " four or five weeks " and promised other leaders that it would be won in three to four days . Now the world is approaching month seven of the on-again, off-again conflict. In a déjà vu moment, Trump recited his favorite talking points to Axios on Thursday: A "big decision" is coming soon, and he might "annihilate" Iran, but the Iranian leadership wants a deal very badly. item.title: Gaza artists honour Macklemore for supporting Palestine
item.description:
Twenty years ago, even Madonna faced radio blacklisting for being overtly political. But in our age of streaming, there’s less excuse for not speaking out It must have come as a surprise to Ed Sheeran when all of his support acts withdrew from the remainder of the US leg of his tour. The American rapper Macklemore had triggered the walkout when he gave an impassioned speech calling for a “free Palestine” on stage and was dropped for doing so. The decision by the remaining acts to drop out in solidarity exposed a deep divide in the modern music industry. Some artists still insist on keeping politics out of music, while others expect music to speak to our perilous times. item.title: Iran-backed Houthi rebels warn against joining Saudi Arabia in Yemen's growing civil war
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said Saturday that its air defenses destroyed a ballistic missile fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels at Riyadh, the first strike on the Saudi fighting with the Iran-backed group reignited this summer. The Saudi-led coalition confirmed the interception hours after the dawn launch. Residents reported hearing an explosion, and journalists saw firefighters extinguish a blaze on the Aramco-branded fuel tank at a depot near King Khalid International Airport. No casualties were reported. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the Houthis also tried to hit civilian infrastructure in Yanbu — the Red Sea terminus of a key Saudi oil pipeline — as well as Taif, Baysh and Farasan, all of which were thwarted. item.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals
item.description:
After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. An in-depth investigation reveals the ‘show of force’ costing American taxpayers millions No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out. Continue reading...

item.title: Man, 82, dies after beach fight with 76-year-old over sunlounger in Greece
item.description:
Row at Athenian riviera resort turned violent after two elderly bathers reportedly argued over shortage of loungers Greek police are investigating the death of an 82-year-old man after a brawl over a sunlounger at a beach on the Athenian riviera. The man had arrived at the popular bathing spot of Vouliagmeni before 10am on Sunday hoping to secure a sunbed, but he soon began arguing with a fellow bather – described by authorities as a “76-year-old man unknown to him” – when it became clear loungers were in short supply. item.title: Iran closes language center in Tehran, France vows response
item.description:
Iranian authorities on Sunday shut down the French Language Centre (CLF) in Tehran, alleging the French embassy-linked institute conducted "illegal acts that violated diplomatic conventions" and "abused its status as a language training facility". France has vowed to take "appropriate measures" in response.

item.description:
